title: JSON in SQL Server: OPENJSON and FOR JSON
description: Shred a JSON payload into relational rows and rebuild it, including indexes on JSON paths.

data.text: An API stores order metadata as JSON in an `nvarchar(max)` column because the shape changes frequently. Write T-SQL that (a) reads the `priority` and `tags` fields from a stored document, (b) explodes an array of line items into rows, and (c) makes `priority` efficiently searchable. Then explain how to return a relational result as nested JSON.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- Sample payload shape
-- {"priority":"high","tags":["vip","gift"],"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":2},{"sku":"B7","qty":1}]}

-- (a) Read scalar fields
SELECT
    OrderId,
    JSON_VALUE(Metadata, '$.priority')                       AS Priority,
    JSON_QUERY(Metadata, '$.tags')                            AS TagsJson
FROM Orders;

-- (b) Explode the items array into rows
SELECT o.OrderId,
       i.sku,
       i.qty
FROM Orders AS o
CROSS APPLY OPENJSON(o.Metadata, '$.items')
    WITH (
        sku nvarchar(50)  '$.sku',
        qty int           '$.qty'
    ) AS i
WHERE JSON_VALUE(o.Metadata, '$.priority') = 'high';

-- (c) Index the hot JSON path with a computed column
ALTER TABLE Orders
    ADD Priority AS (JSON_VALUE(Metadata, '$.priority')) PERSISTED;
GO
CREATE INDEX IX_Orders_Priority ON Orders (Priority) INCLUDE (OrderId);

-- Return relational rows as nested JSON
SELECT
    c.CustomerId,
    c.CustomerName,
    OrderList.Orders
FROM Customers AS c
CROSS APPLY (
    SELECT o.OrderId, o.OrderDate, o.Total
    FROM Orders AS o
    WHERE o.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
    FOR JSON PATH
) AS OrderList(Orders)
FOR JSON PATH, ROOT('result');

data.title: Explanation
data.text: `OPENJSON` with a `WITH` clause is the workhorse: it gives each array element a typed row. Always supply explicit types — `OPENJSON` without a `WITH` clause returns everything as `nvarchar(4000)` and forces implicit conversions downstream. `JSON_VALUE` extracts a scalar; `JSON_QUERY` extracts an object or array as JSON text (use it inside `FOR JSON` so a nested array is not escaped as a string). For searchable fields, a **PERSISTED computed column plus an index** is the standard trick — you cannot index the raw JSON column directly, but the persisted expression is materialised and indexable.
